html:
On 5 December 2006 the army commander, Frank Bainimarama, overthrew the elected government of Laisenia Qarase, Fiji's fourth coup in twenty years.

Unlike the coups of 1987, this one claimed to fight ethnic nationalism and corruption. The military government abolished the Great Council of Chiefs, called all citizens Fijians, and in 2013 imposed a constitution with a single voters' roll.

Bainimarama won elections in 2014 and 2018 but ruled with tight limits on the press and courts. He lost power in 2022 to Rabuka, the leader of 1987. Australia and New Zealand imposed sanctions for years, and Fiji grew closer to China. See Fiji.
sum: On 5 December 2006 the army commander, Frank Bainimarama, overthrew the elected government of Laisenia Qarase, Fiji's fourth coup in twenty years.
